pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome | Milverton Community Primary and Pre-School
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome to Milverton Community Primary School and Preschool
Inspiring every child to achieve their full potential. Nurturing our children to become resilient, respectful and responsible global citizens.
We believe that education is a partnership between parents, children and staff. Education should be fun, engaging, and inspire a lifelong love of learning. Children, like the rest of us, learn so much better when they enjoy what they are doing. At our school we use the values. We care, we aspire, we belong, to create a whole school ethos where everybody feels valued, welcomed and tries to be the best that they can be.
All the adults that work in our school strive to support the happiness and well-being of our children. We are determined to ensure that every child can develop and reach their full potential with a keen focus on strong academic progress and achievement. We believe that our children's mental health and well-being is just as important as their physical well-being and academic achievement. Please see the wellbeing page on our website.
Our beautiful school grounds encourage us to be innovative in utilising the outdoors as a valuable teaching and learning resource through regular forest school and outdoor learning sessions. We have beautiful, mature trees and natural habitats that enable us to inspire environmental awareness in all our pupils. The school was first recognised as an Eco-School in 2006, and we are very proud to be holders of multiple Green Flag Awards ever since. In our latest eco award assessment it was noted that the Eco Committee's assembly presentation demonstrated excellent pupil leadership and helped inspire the whole school to think and act as responsible global citizens.
Our children have many positions of responsibility across the school and are given opportunities to develop their leadership skills. We asked members of our School Council to describe their school.
“It is a friendly and welcoming school with lots of things always going on. We love the fact that we have lots of outdoor space and love the old trees.”
“There is always lots to interest us, loads of clubs and activities and we go on many exciting educational visits out.”
“Our teachers always make our lessons really fun. We really feel part of the school and feel that we belong.”
“The best words that describe our school are awesome, caring, beautiful, friendly, eco-focused, sensational.”
We do hope our website gives you a flavour of the school.
If you have any queries, please contact the school office on
or e-mail office@milvertonprimary.co.uk.

There are two toasties sessions with the first session running from 3:20pm to 4:30pm and the second session running from 4:30pm to 5:30pm.

pageCache.pageTitle: Governors' Pen Portraits | Milverton Community Primary and Pre-School
pageCache.text:
Governors' Pen Portraits
Governors
Linda Burton
I have been on the Board of Governors of Milverton Primary School since September 2017, Vice Chair in 2020 and Chair since September 2021. I am a retired History and Classical Civilisations teacher; my last position was at Wellington School, where I taught for nineteen years during which time I was Head of Lower, then Upper School. I have lived in Milverton since 1985, have two adult sons and three grandchildren, one of whom has just started primary school. The Chair’s primary role is to ensure that the governing board is effective in setting and implementing the school’s direction and strategy, therefore I am responsible for leading the Board and focusing on strategic matters, overseeing the school’s planning and setting high governance standards. I work in partnership with Mrs. Stoddart, offering support, challenge, encouragement and helping ensure that his performance management is rigorous and robust. My role as EYFS Governor is to act as a link between the Governing Board and staff and to report to the Board on topics such as subject delivery, the impact of interventions, attainment and progress and transition.
office@milvertonprimary.co.uk
Emily Weiss
I have been part of the Milverton School community since September 2016 when my eldest daughter joined the school in year 1. I became a Governor in 2019. I currently work in a Leadership role in another local school and as part of my remit, I deliver Safeguarding training and support policy implementation. I hopefully use my educational experience and knowledge to support Milverton in achieving its aims and objectives. Working closely with the Designated Safeguarding Lead, the safeguarding governance role focuses on safeguarding processes and procedures ensuring they are reviewed on a regular basis. This includes ensuring the school has an effective safeguarding policy in place, that safer recruitment practices are followed and the safeguarding training for all school staff and Governors is relevant and up-to-date.
Stephen Penny
I have taught at Milverton Community Primary and Pre-School since September 2013 and was elected as the staff Governor in 2015. I have worked in both Key Stages and am currently in Year 4. I am passionate about teaching and working with the children at Milverton. My role as the staff Governor is to be a conduit between the school staff and the governing body. I am part of the education sub- committee in which I bring my professional knowledge and expertise as well as ensuring that the staff have a voice on the governing body. I thoroughly enjoy my role as staff Governor as I feel that it provides me with further opportunities to work alongside staff, families and our community to ensure that our pupils receive an enriching and inspiring curriculum.
Stephen Jones
My wife and I have lived in Milverton for 7 years and get involved in community projects and support local events. I started my working life as a buyer for J Sainsbury at head office in London and formed Somerdale International in 1990. I now run a food export company based in Wellington exporting British Cheese and Dairy products worldwide. My daughters went to Wellington School and I have grandchildren in Devon and Australia!
Chris Mann
I was elected as a governor to Milverton Primary in late 2022. I have had a house in Milverton since 2007 and retired in 2023 having spent the last thirty years in education teaching Biology. My last position was at Harrow School in London where I taught for the last 20 years; it was here that I also gained significant experience on the pastoral side of school life. At Milverton Primary I sit on the Education Committee and am the link governor for Science and Physical Education.
Fiona Taylor
I am a chartered accountant and the Director of Finance at Wellington School. I became a school governor in 2023 so that I could bring my own experiences of leading a school and hope to support Milverton Primary and Pre-school in ensuring that children at the school are receiving the best opportunities to shape their future.
Clare Adams
I have been a parent of Milverton school since 2021, and my three children have adored their time here. Children are at the heart of my working life as a paediatrician at Musgrove, which I love, and I bring this passion to my governor role which I started in October 2024. As SEND Governor I act as the strategic link between the governing board and the school leadership team regarding SEND provision. I work closely with our SENCO Mrs Meera Pow, to ensure the school’s SEND policy is being implemented effectively, as well as monitoring, challenging and ensuring the school’s statutory duties are met. I aim to support school to keep inclusion at the centre of our work, and ensure that all children with SEND achieve, belong and thrive at Milverton.
Rob Hancock
I was brought up in Wiveliscombe and recently moved to Milverton to retire after a career which took me away from the area. Now that I have the time to devote to giving back, I will endeavour to apply those commercial skills to the school. My own business is running training courses, but that’s as close as I have previously been to mainstream education, so I bring an ‘outside-in’ perspective. I’m also a Parish Councillor where I aim to do my bit to support Milverton’s vibrant community, attractive buildings, and rural life alongside protecting our village infrastructure, charitable works, and social groups, so I will represent the school on the council, and vice versa. The school is integral to our village community today, and to our future here in Milverton and beyond.
Tim McConnell-Wood
As a teacher of Economics and Business Studies at GCSE and A Level, my expertise lies mainly in secondary education. However, most of the schools in which I have worked were all-through schools, giving me valuable insight into the educational journey from the early years through to sixth form. Throughout my career, I have been passionate about helping young people develop not only academically but also socially, emotionally and personally. I firmly believe that education is about preparing children for life as well as learning, and I have a particular interest in pastoral care and the development of the whole child. As a Governor, I look forward to using my experience to support and challenge the leadership team, helping to ensure that every child at the Community Primary School is encouraged to be confident, curious and successful, and is given the very best start in life.
Sue Lucas
I’m a retired Primary School teacher and senior leader. During my career I taught in Key Stage 2, Key Stage 1 and Early Years, including managing and developing a large school based nursery. I finished my career as the Early Years Advisor for a large Multi Academy Trust, working across three different local authorities. Early Years is my absolute passion, so I am delighted to be taking on this focus as part of my role as a school governor. Research shows that “Children learn and develop at a faster rate between birth and age five, than at any other time of their lives, so that their experiences in early years have a major impact on their future life choices.” Early Years Foundation Stage Statutory Framework 2026 So, with this in mind, as a governor with a focus on EYFS, I will report to the board on the school delivery of the vision and pedagogy for this important stage of a child’s life. It has been a privilege to get to know the school through my weekly visits as a volunteer listening to children read and chatting with parents and carers in the playground, when I collect my Grandson from school.
Kieran Neale
My children have attended Milverton throughout their primary years so, when a parent governor position became available, I jumped at the opportunity to give what I can back to the school.
Through my work as a Senior Brand Manager, and decades at the metaphorical marketing coalface, I have significant experience in strategy development, project management and leadership – skills I am pleased to bring to the superb Governing body.
We may not know what the future holds for our children, but we can begin their journey to a confident destination here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Information on Wellbeing | Milverton Community Primary and Pre-School
pageCache.text:
Information on Wellbeing
Emotion Coaching
All staff have received training in Emotion Coaching. This is a technique that involves supporting children to recognise, understand and manage their feelings. It uses the analogy of a clenched fist for the brain, and explains the gradual and cumulative process of children becoming angry or anxious; this is termed 'flipping their lids' and gives them strategies of how they can regulate these upsetting emotions and bring their 'lids' back down.
SHARE Emotion Coaching Sessions
ELSA
These are one to one sessions that children have with a TA trained in Emotional Literacy. The sessions can focus on self-awareness, self-regulation, social skills, self esteem. Usually, these sessions run for half and hour and run to 8 sessions.
Self Regulation Group
This is a group set up by the school's Occupational Therapist that supports children who find regulating their energy levels difficult after playtime and are not ready to concentrate. Children work with a trained TA for 5 to 10 minutes after break time and lunch using strategies to calm their mind and body for learning.
Forest School
For information on our wonderful Forest School sessions please go to our Forest School page.
National Trailblazer Project
Milverton School is part of the National Trailblazer project. Mental Health Support Teams provide early intervention on some mental health and emotional wellbeing issues, such as mild to moderate anxiety. They also support school staff provide a 'whole school' approach' to mental health and wellbeing. The teams will act as a link with local children and young people's mental health services and be supervised by NHS staff.
Wellbeing Team
As a result of the being involved with the Trailblazer project the school are developing a wellbeing team which consists of staff, governors, parents and pupils. This team of people work together to ensure the profile of mental health is raised in the school amongst children and staff.
Hello Yellow Day
Each year we recognise that it's World Mental Health Day by taking part in 'Hello Yellow'. Each class takes part in an activity designed to raise awareness about mental health and the importance of keeping minds healthy, as well as healthy bodies. It's wonderful to see cheerful bursts of yellow across the school! This year on @hello Yellow Day' children learnt about embracing and celebrating our differences, whilst remembering that we all have a lot in common beneath the surface. We also thought about how Milverton School serves as a wonderful, warm community that is here to support each child and all the grown-ups associated with the school.

Special Educational Needs (SEND)
Milverton School SEND Department
All children are special. All children are unique. At Milverton Community Primary School we aim to provide an environment where all pupils feel safe and can flourish. We are committed to providing an education that enables all pupils to make progress with the right level of support, care, and encouragement to achieve their best and become confident individuals living fulfilling lives. Our SENCo is Meera Pow and can be contacted via the school office or send@milvertonprimary.co.uk.
SEND Policies
Somerset Local Offer
This is a website to help families and young people find local infomation and services close to home Somerset Local Offer website
SENDIAS (Somerset Educational Needs and Disability Information, Advice and Support)
This service provides impartial information, advice and support for parent carers and young people (up to the age of 25) about special educational needs and disability (SEND) and to encourage partnership working with schools, colleges, early year providers, the Local Authority and voluntary services. Please visit thier website Somerset SENDIAS
Somerset Parent Carer Forum
Somerset Parent Carer Forum is a support group for Parent Carers and families of children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) in Somerset. For more information, please visit Somerset Parent Carer Forum or their Facebook page https://en-gb.facebook.com/SomersetParentCarerForum/
Their guide to navigating autism, ADHD and other conditions with confidence and compassion is filled with expert advice and Somerset processes. It helps you celebrate your child's unique strengths and become their greatest advocate, whether you are just starting your journey or looking for new ways to help your child flourish, information on the link below is here to empower you every step of the way:
Supporting your Neurodivergent child

pageCache.pageTitle: Severe Weather Procedures | Milverton Community Primary and Pre-School
pageCache.text:
Severe Weather Procedures
In the event of severe weather conditions such as heavy snow or ice, it may be necessary to close the school for the safety or pupils and staff. The school may partially open if there is enough staff and non-curriculum activities will be planned for the day.
If a decision is made in the morning to close the school, parents will be notified by a Parentmail text and email, and it will also be published on this website.
If the weather worsens during a school day and the decision is made to close the school, parents will be contacted via Parentmail to collect their children. For those children who travel on school transport, the school will ensure there is somebody at home to meet the child. We will keep children at school until they can be collected.
